questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them without training can make a minor injury worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press down on the wound to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: After you pass a vehicle moving in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back into your lane.

questions.question: What should you do to enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can watch the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always let other traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: The longer distance needed for large vehicles to stop.
The shorter distance needed for large vehicles to stop.
The quieter noise from larger vehicles.
The higher speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance needed for large vehicles to stop.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Other drivers must stay where the truck driver can see them and where they can see traffic ahead.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect them to do?

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and may run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Keep your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When you can, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: When you meet a car with bright headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear from the driver's view or are so close they prevent the truck from stopping and turning safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to drive behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear from the driver's view or are so close they prevent the truck from stopping and turning safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are so close they prevent the truck driver from stopping or turning safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Use only the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. You may need to look several times. Watch the traffic in front of you and in the lane next to you.

questions.question: What effect does a blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent have?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol level nearly doubles your risk of being in a fatal crash.

questions.question: How much lane width are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let this traffic merge safely.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does this mean?

options.text: Passing is permitted from the left.
Passing is permitted from the right.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down faster.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, your reactions slow down. You feel more confident and make more mistakes.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs show construction areas. Drive carefully.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what type of headlights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What colors do warning signs use to show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look when driving?

options.text: 10 to 15 seconds.
100 to 150 yards.
One to two blocks.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 15 seconds.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden moves and stay safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
You must treat the intersection like a stop sign.
You may not go until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must treat the intersection like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are angry about something that happened at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you will not think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck has room to stop.
So other drivers have room to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left, but oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for a driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes are clear and you can safely make the turn.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Take a different route.
Drive the same way you do on dry roads.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car takes longer to stop.

questions.question: To be ready for anything ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and roadsides.
questions.explanation: Look for problems before you reach them. Scan the whole road and the sides, not just straight ahead.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
See what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it could be unsafe.
Lanes go in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving the same direction. You may cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Many car crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the road conditions. Always drive at safe speeds and slow down when conditions are not perfect.
